pr_title: Avoid inferring RequiredAttribute for properties of types in the fram…
pr_body:
…ework

* Validation in MVC is recursive, but will short-circuit if none of the sub-properties on a given instance require validation.

* In 3.1, MVC added a feature where it will annotate non-nullable properties and parameters with a Required attribute in it's model metadata. Validation would then validate that the property was assigned a non-null value.

In tandem, the 2nd bullet point makes validation perform very poorly for framework or library types that have been annotated with non-null attributes. In particular, when the nullability does not describe what the outcome should be when binding a model, but rather the nullability behavior of a well-formed instance. A very tactical change we could make here is to avoid annotating properties on types declared in the framework with the implicit [Required].

It's important to know that the implicit Required feature does not apply to generic types (MVC does not know how to interpret nullability + generic types), so we don't have a scenario where a framework type could hold a reference to a user type at compile time (e.g List<Person>).

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/36919

issue_context.title: MVC model validation in default configuration is very slow if models contain delegate properties
comments:
I took a look at this behavior and you can disable this option to fix the performance:

```C#
s.AddMvc(o => o.SuppressImplicitRequiredAttributeForNonNullableReferenceTypes = true);
```

With nullable reference types turned on, MVC will generate am implicit `[Required]` attribute for any non nullable reference types.
